title: Material properties of biomolecular condensates emerge from nanoscale dynamics.
authors: Galvanetto, Nicola; Ivanovic, Milos T; Del Grosso, Simone A; Chowdhury, Aritra; Sottini, Andrea; Nettels, Daniel; Best, Robert B; Schuler, Benjamin
one_liner_zh: 该文结合实验与原子模拟，揭示无序蛋白凝聚体黏度源于纳米尺度链动力学与接触寿命，建立了聚合物物理预测框架，直接关联IDR相分离中的PPI动态机制，对互作机制建模有重要启发。
abstract: Biomolecular condensates form by phase separation of biological polymers and have important functions in the cell - functions that are inherently linked to their physical properties at different scales. A notable aspect of such membraneless organelles is that their viscoelastic properties can vary by orders of magnitude, but it has remained unclear how these pronounced differences are rooted in the nanoscale dynamics at the molecular level. Here we investigate a series of condensates formed by complex coacervation of highly charged disordered proteins and polypeptides that span about two orders of magnitude in bulk viscosity. We find that their viscosity is highly correlated with protein translational diffusion and nano- to microsecond chain dynamics. Remarkably, analytical relations from polymer physics can predict condensate viscosity from diffusivity and chain dynamics, and vice versa, even for more hydrophobic disordered proteins and for synthetic polyelectrolytes, indicating a mechanistic link across several decades of length- and timescales. Atomistic simulations reveal that the observed differences in friction - a key quantity underlying these relations - reflect differences in inter-residue contact lifetimes as a function of arginine content and salt concentration, leading to the vastly different dynamics among condensates. The rapid exchange of inter-residue contacts we observe may be a general mechanism for preventing dynamic arrest in compartments densely packed with polyelectrolytes, such as the cell nucleus.
abstract_zh: 生物分子凝聚体通过生物聚合物的相分离（phase separation）形成，在细胞中具有重要功能——这些功能与其在不同尺度上的物理性质密切相关。这类无膜细胞器的一个显著特点是其粘弹性可相差数个数量级，但至今尚不清楚这些显著差异如何在分子层面的纳米尺度动力学中扎根。在此，我们研究了一系列由高电荷无序蛋白质和多肽复合凝聚（complex coacervation）形成的凝聚体，其体相粘度跨越约两个数量级。我们发现，这些凝聚体的粘度与蛋白质平移扩散及纳秒至微秒尺度的链动力学高度相关。值得注意的是，聚合物物理中的解析关系能够从扩散率和链动力学预测凝聚体粘度，反之亦然，甚至适用于更疏水的无序蛋白质和合成聚电解质，这表明在跨越数个数量级的长度和时间尺度上存在机制性联系。原子级模拟揭示，观察到的摩擦差异——这些关系背后的关键量——反映了残基间接触寿命的差异，这些差异取决于精氨酸含量和盐浓度，从而导致凝聚体间截然不同的动力学行为。我们观察到的残基间接触的快速交换可能是一种通用机制，用于防止在充满聚电解质的区室（如细胞核）中发生动态停滞。
